function.name: introduction_greet
function.description: Generate a greeting message introducing a person and their relationship to another individual. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name of the person being introduced.

relationship.description: The type of relationship to the related person.

related_person.description: The name of the person to whom the first person is related.

include_relationship.description: A flag to indicate whether to include the relationship in the greeting message.

message.content: I don’t personally know anyone named Daniel, but I can certainly help you craft an introduction or find information about a specific Daniel if you give me a bit more detail—such as his full name, profession, or the context in which you’d like to introduce him.
message.reasoning: User asks: "do you know Daniel?" We need to respond appropriately. According to policy, we should not claim personal knowledge or familiarity. We can say we don't personally know him. But we can ask clarifying question: "Which Daniel?" Or "Do you want me to introduce someone named Daniel?" The user didn't specify context. We could ask for clarification. Also we might mention we don't have personal acquaintances. So answer: "I don't personally know anyone named Daniel, but I can help with introductions if you provide details." That seems safe.
